definitions.explanation: So closely connected to something else that the two cannot meaningfully be separated. A formal, abstract word used in writing about concepts, rights, relationships, or processes that must be treated as a unified whole.

examples.japanese: {心|こころ}と{体|からだ}は{不可分|ふかぶん}だ。
{自由|じゆう}と{責任|せきにん}は{不可分|ふかぶん}の{関係|かんけい}にある。
examples.english: Freedom and responsibility are in an inseparable relationship.

examples.japanese: {言語|げんご}と{文化|ぶんか}は{不可分|ふかぶん}なものだと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: Language and culture are said to be inseparable.

examples.japanese: {経済|けいざい}{発展|はってん}と{環境|かんきょう}{保護|ほご}は{不可分|ふかぶん}の{課題|かだい}として{議論|ぎろん}されている。
examples.english: Economic development and environmental protection are being discussed as inseparable issues.

notes:
Composed of {不|ふ} (not) + {可|か} (able, possible) + {分|ぶん} (divide, part). Literally 'not-able-to-divide' — meaning something that cannot be split apart. A written, conceptual word that almost always appears with {の}{関係|かんけい} (relationship of inseparability) or in the form {不可分|ふかぶん}なX.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {不可分|ふかぶん}の{関係|かんけい}: an inseparable relationship (the most common phrase)
- {不可分|ふかぶん}の{一部|いちぶ}: an inseparable part (of something)
- {不可分|ふかぶん}の{存在|そんざい}: an inseparable presence
- {不可分|ふかぶん}な{問題|もんだい}: an inseparable problem
- AとBは{不可分|ふかぶん}だ: A and B are inseparable
- AとBは{不可分|ふかぶん}に{結|むす}びついている: A and B are inseparably linked

USAGE:
Typically used to claim that two things cannot be discussed, solved, or understood in isolation from each other. Common subjects include abstract pairs: mind/body, language/culture, rights/duties, economy/environment. The word is neutral or approving — it frames the connection as essential, not as an awkward entanglement.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {切|き}り{離|はな}せない: cannot be separated — an everyday native-Japanese equivalent, more conversational.
- {一体|いったい}: united as one, integrated — emphasizes that two things are one body, rather than that they cannot be divided.
- {表裏|ひょうり}{一体|いったい}: two sides of the same coin — a four-character idiom for things that are different faces of one whole.

ANTONYMS:
- {可分|かぶん}: divisible — the direct opposite, but far less common in everyday use.
